learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows the acquisition of the rest of the degree competencies.

Ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods, and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to plan, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate design methods.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design, and research and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment, and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects of their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and to society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.
Uses integral calculus for multivariable functions in solving geometric and physical problems.
Develops and interprets Fourier series for periodic and non-periodic functions.
Makes decisions and evaluates the possible consequences of the selected alternative.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of language, in writing.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and making correct use of language orally.
Uses vector calculus in solving geometric and physical problems.
Coordinates their work with other team members, contributes to their team in the development of tasks to be performed and the creation of a good working environment.
Uses multivariable differential calculus for error estimation, function optimization, and the calculation of gradients and their applications.

teaching_methods: Development, writing and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs, individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Lectures by the professor in the classroom, in participatory classes, covering concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Computer simulation practices, individually and/or in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices
Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, technical presentation and defense

assessment_rules: The final grade for assessments including control points is calculated as 0.25 multiplied by the grade of the first control point plus 0.75 multiplied by the recovery grade. Project evaluation is continuous, based on team meetings with tutors and experts. One week before the final report submission, work is analyzed to identify and communicate areas for improvement. The final version of the report with corrected aspects serves as the recovery.
